Export a selection

Source: R/exports.R
soil_export.Rd

Submits the selection as an export (POST /exports): the API writes every record of the selection, up to limits$max_export_observations observations (10,000,000; soil_capabilities()), into a zip of files, then keeps it for 7 days. Exports are the way to large selections: the synchronous reads (soil_observations(), soil_features()) are refused above limits$max_sync_observations (1,000,000). Rule of thumb: size the selection with soil_summary(); below about 200,000 observations read synchronously, above it export (a whole-WoSIS wide CSV export takes about 9 minutes on the server, 88 MB zipped). Exports also give GeoPackage and Shapefile files for GIS.

Usage

soil_export(
  soil = soil_session(),
  datasets = NULL,
  variables = NULL,
  bbox = NULL,
  country = NULL,
  geometry = "any",
  layer = "all",
  view = "raw",
  profile_type = NULL,
  components = NULL,
  min_cumulative_percent = NULL,
  format = c("gpkg", "geojson", "csv", "tsv", "shp"),
  content = c("all", "features"),
  layout = c("wide", "long"),
  wait = TRUE,
  timeout = 3600,
  poll = 5,
  download = wait,
  dir = NULL,
  unzip = TRUE,
  progress = interactive()
)

Arguments

soil

A session; the default session when omitted. Client-side: not sent to the API.

datasets

Catalog dataset codes ("wosis_points", "wise_profiles", "soter_profiles", "soter_polygons", "sotwis_polygons", "sotwis_components", "sotwis_estimates", see soil_datasets()); NULL (the API default) selects every dataset, usually above the limit of synchronous reads. API field datasets.

variables

Source codes ("ORGC", "CLAY") or canonical property keys ("organic_carbon"), see soil_variables(); NULL returns every variable. With variables the column set is fixed by the request, so every page has the same columns. API field variables.

bbox

c(xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax) in WGS84 degrees (longitude, latitude). API field bbox.

country

Countries as ISO 3166 alpha-2 or alpha-3 codes or names, case-insensitive (the API resolves them). API field country.

geometry

"any", "point" (profiles) or "polygon" (map units). API field geometry.

layer

"all" horizons, or "first": the first horizon(s) of each profile with first_layer_status and profile_markings (see soil_first_layer()). API field layer.

view

"raw": the ISRIC mirror as stored (sent explicitly); "revised": the decided rules of the revised view applied by the API in the response (see soil_revised_rules()). API field view.

profile_type

Profiles by the source's own type term: "synthetic" (KENSOTER), "virtual" (Upper Tana), "none" (no type in the source record), all selecting or all excluded with a "!" prefix (c("!synthetic", "!virtual")); NULL keeps every profile. API field profile_type.

components

Components of multi-component map units (SOTWIS, SOTER polygons): NULL (the API default, "representative"), "representative" (largest proportion_percent), "all", or "cumulative" (by decreasing proportion until min_cumulative_percent). API field components.

min_cumulative_percent

Threshold of components = "cumulative", 0 to 100 (required with it, refused without it). API field min_cumulative_percent.

format

File format: "gpkg" (GeoPackage, the default), "geojson", "csv", "tsv", or "shp" (Shapefile: only with content = "features"). The formats are those of soil_capabilities()$exports. API field format.

content

"all" (the features and their observations) or "features" (the features only). API field content.

layout

Shape of the observations table: "wide" (one row per horizon) or "long" (one row per observation); not sent with content = "features". API field layout.

wait

Wait for the export to end (TRUE), or return at once with its job_id (FALSE). Client-side: not sent to the API.

timeout

Seconds to wait for the export (default one hour); the export continues on the server after a timeout. Client-side: not sent to the API.

poll

Seconds between two polls of the export (at least 2). Client-side: not sent to the API.

download

Download the zip once the export is completed (needs wait = TRUE). Client-side: not sent to the API.

dir

Directory of the downloads; NULL uses the option soilhub.export_dir, the environment variable SOILHUB_EXPORT_DIR, else file.path(tempdir(), "soilhub-exports"). Client-side: not sent to the API.

unzip

Unzip the download into <dir>/<job_id>/. Client-side: not sent to the API.

progress

Show the progress of the export (fraction written) and of the download: progress bars in an interactive session, else one message per change of status. Client-side: not sent to the API.

Value

A soil_export (a list): job_id, status (queued, running, completed, failed, cancelled), progress (percent), observation_count (the observations of the selection, counted at submission), records (the records written per table, once completed), file_size_bytes, expires_at (POSIXct UTC), error_message, format, content, layout, request (the body sent), selection (the selection arguments), and after the download zip (path), files (names), dir (the unzipped directory) and metadata (the parsed metadata.json, read by soil_metadata(), soil_citations(), soil_columns(), soil_revised_rules()).

Details

The zip holds metadata.json (the request, the record counts, the datasets with citation and licence, the variables, the typing of the wide columns, the warnings and the revised rules) and two tables joined on feature_id: features (one record per feature, with its geometry) and, with content = "all", observations in the layout asked (wide: one row per horizon, every variable column on every row; long: one row per observation), without geometry. Files by format: "gpkg" export.gpkg (layers features and observations); "geojson" features.geojson, observations.geojson; "csv"/"tsv" features.csv (geometry as WKT in geometry_wkt), observations.csv (nested values as JSON text); "shp" (features only) features_points.* and features_polygons.*.

With wait = TRUE (the default) the function polls the export every poll seconds until it ends, downloads the zip into dir and unzips it into <dir>/<job_id>/; read the tables with soil_export_read(). With wait = FALSE it returns at once: keep the job_id, the API keeps no list of a user's exports, and resume later, also in another R session, with soil_export_wait(soil, job_id) then soil_export_download().

Rights: soil:read. Capabilities: complete_exports (checked at soil_connect()); revised_view, profile_type_filter, component_selection as for the reads.

See also

soil_export_read(), soil_summary() to size a selection.

Other exports: soil_export_from_error(), soil_export_read(), soil_export_status()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
soil <- soil_connect()
x <- soil_export(soil, datasets = "wosis_points", country = "BRA", format = "csv")
x
obs <- soil_export_read(x)
features <- soil_export_read(x, "features")
soil_citations(x)

# submit now, collect later (keep the job id)
x <- soil_export(soil, datasets = "wosis_points", format = "gpkg", wait = FALSE)
x$job_id
x <- soil_export_wait(soil, x$job_id)
x <- soil_export_download(soil, x)
} # }
